newsitem.title: CHINA: China aims to double ship output value by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China aims to double ship output value by 2000.

text.p: China is hoping to double its ship output value to 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) by the year 2000, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

Output value of state-owned China State Shipbuilding Corp (CSSC) was expected to grow by 16 percent a year in the final five years of the century, Xinhua quoted Wang Rongsheng, general manager of the company, as saying.
China Shipbuilding would capture 10 percent of the world shipbuilding market in 2000, double the five percent share it held last year, Wang said, adding that the firm would double that again by 2010.
CSSC would expand output capacity to four million tonnes a year in 2000 while actual production was seen hitting three million tonnes, Wang said.
The company would export about two-thirds of output every year and rake in an annual $1.2-1.5 billion of foreign currency from shipbuilding, ship repair and machinery exports, he said.
Profits and taxes for CSSC would total 3.0 billion yuan in 2000, he said.
The company expected to import about 20 percent of its raw materials, he said but gave no further details.
